editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a tiny submarine with the one guy you absolutely cannot stand. That is exactly what happens to Lt. Tommy Knowlton. He starts off on a romantic getaway in Italy where he falls hard for Jean Standish. The only problem? She is already married and happens to be the daughter of the man in charge of his ship. It creates a messy love triangle that makes the air feel heavy even before they dive underwater. The vibe is a mix of old-school romance and high-stakes military stress, making you feel the heat of their rivalry as the story unfolds.

What really makes this one work is the tension between the two lead men. When a tough call during a battle leads to a tragedy, the anger on the ship boils over. While some of the acting feels a bit stiff by today's standards, the pacing keeps you interested. If you love classic war stories with a lot of heart, you should definitely give this a try. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored version.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head during a final, dangerous mission. After fighting with the Commander for most of the movie, Tommy finally proves his loyalty and courage under pressure. The Commander realizes that his strictness almost cost them everything and acknowledges Tommy's skill. The romantic tension with Jean is settled as they realize their feelings cannot overcome their duties. They all survive the depths, and the two men finally find a way to respect each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood dramas and submarine movies.
